title: GPU Guardian Cockpit — Scenario Sandbox & Cost-aware Burst Composer
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact ops cockpit for Dedicated GPU pools that combines a scenario sandbox (what-if surge/load simulations) with a cost-aware burst composer. The feature lets operators prototype changes to burst capacity, burst duration, autoscale hysteresis, and fallback model routing, and immediately see simulated latency, throughput, and per-minute cost impact across a chosen time window and region. It should integrate with rollouts so a designer or SRE can preview canary steps and emergency-fallback behaviors before applying policies to a pool.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox UI prototype (Figma) demonstrates at least three scenario presets (traffic spike, steady growth, noisy bursts) and allows edit/save of parameters
Cost simulator overlays token-per-second cost, projected 1-hour and 24-hour spend delta, and SLO violation probability based on historical latency distribution
Burst Composer allows users to set burst size (GPUs or vCPU-equivalent), max burst duration, cooldown, and priority rules; changes can be exported as a rollout patch
Rollout preview shows staged progression (canary percentages/time windows), and a simulated fallback to cheaper model variants with expected quality delta noted
Components meet accessibility contrast and keyboard navigation standards and have documented ARIA roles
design_notes: Prioritize a compact horizontal canvas to fit into existing pool detail pages; offer ’Expand to Sandbox’ for full-screen experimentation
Use a layered visualization: top timeline for simulated traffic, middle heatmap for node utilization, bottom cost/probability band for SLO risk
Adopt tokenized presets (Spike, Ramp, Noisy) — users can drag sliders or draw on the timeline to sculpt load
Expose a JSON export for the composed burst policy that maps directly to the runtime policy schema (for ENG validation)
Default safe preset applies conservative cooldown and enforces a maximum burst-to-reserved ratio to protect commitments
attachments: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prs/pull/2345 -- placeholder PR for export schema mapping

accessibility_considerations: Color-blind friendly palette for heatmaps and cost bands
Screen-reader friendly summaries for simulated outcomes
ux_research_findings: Ops interviews (n=6) show frequent manual experiments in staging to validate burst policies; primary pain point is lack of quick cost projection
SREs want the ability to store and reuse scenario presets per customer/pool
Concerns about accidental application of aggressive bursts — users prefer an explicit 'dry-run' and required acknowledgement when exceeding commit thresholds
mock_feedback_summary: PM: include committed-capacity guardrails and clearer language for quality tradeoffs
Eng: exportable JSON must match runtime schema; will add server-side validation and a dry-run API
Design: reduce visual noise in small view, promote expand-to-fullscreen for deep experimentation
